facts.metric: Is there a federal inheritance tax on the recipient?
facts.value: No federal inheritance tax exists
facts.note: The federal transfer tax is an estate tax on the decedent's estate, not a tax on the beneficiary.

facts.value: Fair market value at date of death (step-up)
facts.note: IRS Publication 551 restates 26 U.S.C. §1014: basis is fair market value at date of death. Alternative valuation date available under §2032.

facts.metric: 2026 long-term capital gain breakpoints, married filing jointly
facts.value: 0% up to $98,900 taxable income; 15% up to $613,700; 20% above
3.8% on net investment income above $250,000 MFJ / $200,000 single MAGI
facts.note: Applies to rents and capital gains; excluded gain on a principal residence is also excluded from NIIT.

facts.value: 27.5 years, straight line
facts.note: Only the building is depreciable; land is not.

facts.metric: §121 exclusion on sale of a principal residence
facts.note: Requires 2 of 5 years of use and ownership.

facts.value: Available for real property held for productive use or investment
facts.note: Does not apply to a principal residence.

facts.value: None

facts.value: None
